# Edit project files beside your agent in Paneflow

> Open and correct a file in Files, then review the edit in Changes. If your agent edits the same file, choose which version to keep.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/blog/files-sidebar

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.

     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

The **Files** tab in Paneflow brings the project tree and an editor beside your agent's terminal. Read the code it just changed, adjust a configuration value, or correct a line, then save without leaving Paneflow.

> **Updated guide.** This article originally announced the Files sidebar in Paneflow 0.3.6. It now describes the integrated editor in Paneflow 0.17.5.

## Open, edit, and save a file

1. Select the project tab, then open **Files** in the dock. The tree shows files from that checkout, including when you use a [worktree](/docs/worktrees).
2. Open the text file you want to edit and check its path. The agent's terminal stays visible while you edit.
3. Make your correction, then save with `Ctrl+S` (`Cmd+S` on macOS). The unsaved indicator clears when saving succeeds.

Use `Ctrl+Z` to undo an edit and `Ctrl+Shift+Z` to redo it. On macOS, use `Cmd` instead of `Ctrl`. `Ctrl+Y` also redoes on Windows and Linux. If you undo after saving, save again to write the new state to disk.

Next, open [Changes to review the diff](/blog/diff-viewer) against the latest commit (`HEAD`). This view reads files on disk, so your edits appear there after you save.

## Read changes through Git markers

Git markers in the editor gutter identify lines changed relative to `HEAD`. Select a marker to read the previous text or copy it with **Copy** when available.

**Revert** restores the block in the editor. You can undo that restoration with `Ctrl+Z`, and you need to save to write it to disk. This lets you remove a specific change while keeping the file's other corrections.

## When another process edits the same file

Your agent or another editor can write to a file already open in Files. If you have no unsaved edits, Paneflow reloads the disk content. Otherwise, it shows a conflict and blocks saving until you choose a version:

- **Keep mine** keeps your text in the editor. Saving afterward replaces the disk version with that content.
- **Reload** loads the disk version and discards your unsaved edits.

If you need parts of both versions, copy your edits before choosing **Reload**, then reapply them to the reloaded file. Paneflow does not automatically merge the two versions.

## If you cannot edit or save

A file marked read-only opens with editing disabled. Very long lines can also make a file read-only. Binary files, files over the size limit, and files that are not UTF-8 do not open in the text editor; use a tool suited to their format.

If saving fails, the edits visible in the editor are not saved. Copy them before fixing the reported problem: permissions, a missing folder, or a full disk. Then try saving again.

Once the correction is saved, review the diff in Changes and run the relevant tests in the project's terminal.
